title: Get comfortable with data
description: Use AI to explain spreadsheet formulas, clean sample data, and check analytical conclusions.

sections.title: Explain the structure before asking for a formula
sections.body: Describe column meanings, data types, and the result you need. Provide a small fictional example with an expected answer. Specify the spreadsheet product because functions can differ. Ask the assistant to explain a formula in plain language so you can judge whether it matches your intention.
bullets: Check regional date and number formats.
Clarify how blanks, duplicates, and zero values should behave.

sections.title: Test transformations on a copy
sections.body: Keep an untouched original. Try cleaning or calculation steps on a sample that includes edge cases, such as missing values and repeated rows. Check before-and-after totals. A formula that works for the first row may fail on mixed formats or a larger range.
bullets: Verify formulas with manually calculated examples.
Watch for changed identifiers and leading zeros.

sections.title: Interpret results carefully
sections.body: Ask what assumptions an analysis makes and which alternative explanations remain. Correlation does not establish cause. Check sample size, definitions, units, and time periods before making a decision. Use an appropriate analytical tool for the calculation and AI to help explain or inspect the method.
bullets: Do not upload sensitive datasets without approval.

example.title: A useful test case
example.text: Before accepting a formula for average order value, test three orders, a refund, and a blank row. Decide whether refunds belong in revenue and which rows count as orders. The business definition comes before the formula.

exercise: Create five fictional rows and calculate an expected total by hand. Ask for a formula and test whether it handles a blank and a duplicate correctly.

faq.question: Can I trust a spreadsheet formula from AI?
faq.answer: Treat it as a draft. Test normal inputs and edge cases, and understand the formula before relying on it.

faq.question: Can AI replace statistical expertise?
faq.answer: No. AI can assist with explanations and code, but the design, assumptions, and interpretation still require appropriate expertise.

sources.name: ICO: Artificial intelligence and data protection
